extracted.intended_audience: sellers offering negative-option/subscription features, their compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rule provisions governing sellers' disclosures, consent, recordkeeping, and cancellation mechanisms for negative-option (automatic renewal/auto-enroll) features under the FTC's Click-to-Cancel rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of amount and frequency of charges
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule requires sellers to disclose “The amount (or range of costs) the consumer will be Charged and, if applicable, the frequency of the Charges a consumer will incur unless the consumer takes timely steps to prevent or stop those Charges.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must state the amount or range and, if applicable, how often charges will recur. This disclosure is a material term under §425.4 and should be provided proximate to consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of all material terms including cancellation policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose all material terms (including material policies concerning cancellation) so consumers have the information necessary to effectively cancel the negative option feature (§425.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission expects §425.4, the prohibition on misrepresentations (§425.3), and the simple cancellation mechanism (§425.6) together to ensure important information is easy to find and retain. Disclosures should make cancellation information clear and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retention/use of payment information without consumer consent
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation of section 5 for a seller to retain and use a consumer's payment information without the consumer's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sellers must obtain consent before retaining/using payment credentials for future charges; this principle has been applied in FTC enforcement (e.g., Classic Closeouts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer choice to autofill billing after disclosures (timing of autofill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under ROSCA-related authority, consumers must be given the choice to autofill billing information or provide billing information only after the required disclosures have been provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may allow autofill but must ensure the consumer is given that choice after disclosures; the timing of offering autofill relative to disclosures matters to compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: “The disclosure must use diction and syntax understandable to ordinary consumers.” The Commission declined to replace this phrasing with a different wording and noted that in audio contexts 'diction and syntax' are clearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language, sentence structure, and phrasing (including audio diction/syntax) that ordinary consumers will understand; plain-language principles apply, especially where audio disclosures are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express, unambiguously affirmative consent to negative-option feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature (separately from other transaction terms); §425.5(a)(1) and §425.5(c) allow compliance through a check box, signature, or other substantially similar method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent must be clear and affirmative; obtaining express informed consent separately means consumers agree separately to the negative option feature and the sale. The Rule allows checkboxes or comparable mechanisms but contemplates separate, explicit assent to the negative-option feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear-and-conspicuous disclosure proximate to consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust, clear and conspicuous disclosure proximate to the consumer's consent is required to prevent deception; some commenters argued such a proximate disclosure should be sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place material negative-option disclosures close to where the consumer gives consent (proximate to the consent mechanism). Avoid burying terms; do not include information that interferes with or undermines the negative-option disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of consents and relevant records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers are subject to recordkeeping requirements for consents (and related records); failure to maintain required records (absent an applicable technological exemption) is a violation of the Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records demonstrating express informed consent for the required retention period. The Commission considered comments about burden and suggested alternative retention windows, but emphasized that if a seller cannot satisfy a technological exemption and does not maintain records, it violates the Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple cancellation mechanism requirement (§425.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must provide a simple mechanism for consumers to cancel the negative option feature (§425.6). Consumers and advocates urged cancellation to be 'as easy to cancel as to sign up' (e.g., one-click cancellation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation mechanisms must be quick, easy to find, and not impose undue steps. The Commission defines 'simple mechanism' through §425.6 and supporting guidance/caselaw and expects sellers not to create needless hurdles or labyrinthine flows to obstruct cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation must be available through the same medium used to purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: For online cancellation, §425.6(c)(1) required sellers to provide a simple cancellation mechanism through the same medium consumers used to purchase the negative option feature (the Commission also made a conforming change to add 'consent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a consumer purchased online, the cancellation mechanism must be available online (and similarly for in-person, phone, mail, chat, etc.). The method should require no more steps than the sign-up and be as easy to find.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation applies only to the negative-option feature (does not void whole contract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation under the Rule applies only to the negative option portion of a subscription/contract and not to the entire contract; when a consumer cancels, other contract terms continue until expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sellers should not interpret cancellation as termination of unrelated contract terms; the Rule is aimed at stopping recurring charges associated with the negative-option feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow reasonable authentication/verification prior to cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters insisted reasonable authentication and verification procedures should be allowed prior to cancellation to ensure only authorized persons make changes to an account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sellers may require reasonable identity verification to prevent unauthorized/accidental cancellations, but authentication procedures must not be so burdensome that they frustrate or effectively prevent legitimate cancellations. Balance is required to avoid accidental or malicious cancellations while preserving simplicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using complicated sign-up or shipping practices to frustrate cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission noted concerns that sellers might create complicated signup procedures or delay shipment of goods until the end of trial periods to justify or cause complex cancellation mechanisms; sellers must comply with simple cancellation requirements notwithstanding such practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design of the sign-up flow cannot be used to justify complex cancellations. Practices like delaying shipment to reduce cancellation timeframes or otherwise impede consumers may support findings of deception and violate the Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresentations of material facts or terms (including cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rule prohibits misrepresentations of material facts or terms, including those pertaining to cancellation (§425.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sellers must avoid false or misleading statements about material terms, including how to cancel, costs, renewal, and other negative-option features. Misrepresentations can trigger enforcement actions.
